The script itself contains a heredoc, so write it with an outer heredoc that uses a different end word (SCRIPT). Type this at the prompt:

cat > generate.sh <<'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
source ./vars.env
cat > app.conf <<EOF
# app.conf - generated by generate.sh, do not edit by hand
[app]
name = $APP_NAME
environment = $APP_ENV
listen = 0.0.0.0:$APP_PORT
url = http://localhost:$APP_PORT/

[logging]
format = \$remote_addr "\$request" \$status
EOF
SCRIPT

- <<'SCRIPT' ... SCRIPT     quoted: everything in between goes into generate.sh exactly as typed
- source ./vars.env         loads APP_NAME, APP_PORT and APP_ENV when generate.sh runs
- cat > app.conf <<EOF      unquoted: $APP_NAME etc. are replaced by their values when the script runs
- \$remote_addr             the backslash keeps a $ that belongs to the log format

Check it: bash generate.sh && diff app.conf app.conf.example && echo same
(Or open the script with `edit generate.sh` and type the lines between the SCRIPT markers.)
